23. Case study: describing the same population across two sites

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-23-case-table1.Rmd
book-23-case-table1.Rmd

What you will learn

Describe a shared study population with one column per site and a total, using baseline values, common categories and explicit missing counts.

You need: the Opal login from Getting started and the lab lesson. This chapter uses the two Synthea sites.

Research question

What are the age, sex and baseline haemoglobin characteristics of people entering at their first haemoglobin measurement? We build the descriptive table that opens most study reports, often called “Table 1”. The two Synthea sites contain disjoint halves of the same people, so their people can be added without duplication.

library(dsOMOPClient)
two_conns <- ds.omop.login(rep("https://localhost:8443", 2), user = "administrator",
  password = "password",
  server = c("north", "south"),
  resource = c(north = "omop.synthea_north", south = "omop.synthea_south"))$conns

Confirm the measurement and units at both sites 

hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Hemoglobin", domain = "Measurement", conns = two_conns)$pooled
selected <- hits[trimws(hits$concept_name) == "Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood", ]
selected[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "standard_concept", "vocabulary_id")]
concept_id concept_name standard_concept vocabulary_id
3000963 Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood S LOINC 
hb_id <- selected$concept_id
unit_counts <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = hb_id,
  conns = two_conns)$per_site
do.call(rbind, lapply(names(unit_counts), function(site)
  data.frame(Site = site, unit_counts[[site]][c("value", "concept_name", "n")])))
Site value concept_name n
north 8713 gram per deciliter 50
south 8713 gram per deciliter 50 
hb_set <- omop_concept_set(hb_id)
saveRDS(hb_set, "baseline-haemoglobin.rds")

The shared concept is 3000963, and both sites record 8713, gram per deciliter (g/dL). Each site reports the band 50–54 rows. Adding the band floors gives 100; it does not mean there are exactly 100 measurements. Meaning and units must agree before pooling, not merely the displayed name.

Use only information available at entry

Completed age is measured at the first haemoglobin date. Choose haemoglobin on that date, with no positive tolerance; an all-history mean would include future values and would not describe baseline. Sex is the recorded female/male category; omop_sex() represents it as F/M, labelled Female/Male in the report below.

hb <- omop_event("measurement", hb_set, unit = omop_unit(8713L))
characterise <- omop_study(hb, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(
  age = omop_age_at("index"), sex = omop_sex(),
  age_band = omop_number_bins(omop_age_at("index"), breaks = c(0, 18, 121),
    labels = c("under 18", "adult")),
  haemoglobin = omop_value_at_index("measurement", hb_set,
    tolerance = c(-90, 0), unit = omop_unit(8713L))))
result <- recipe_execute(characterise, out = c(baseline = "D_baseline"), conns = two_conns)
columns <- recipe_codebook(result)[[1]]$columns
age_column <- match("age_band", columns$name)
data.frame(Age_group = columns$levels[[age_column]]$labels)
Age_group
under 18
adult

Both sites use the declared age groups under 18 and adult, including any unused level. The same definition and index are required for comparable columns. The 90-day lookback cannot add earlier haemoglobin here because entry is the first haemoglobin; its selected value is the baseline reading itself.

Assemble the descriptive table from released aggregates

For each numeric variable, ds.mean() supplies its mean and nonmissing count; ds.var() supplies variance, whose square root is the standard deviation (SD). For categories, percentages use all people in that site, with missingness shown as its own row. No patient rows are combined locally.

describe <- function(connections) {
  aggregate_mean <- function(column) dsBaseClient::ds.mean(paste0("D_baseline$", column),
    type = "combine", datasources = connections)$Global.Mean
  variance <- function(column) dsBaseClient::ds.var(paste0("D_baseline$", column),
    type = "combine", datasources = connections)$Global.Variance
  age <- aggregate_mean("age"); lab <- aggregate_mean("haemoglobin")
  n <- age[1, "Ntotal"]
  numeric_text <- function(x, v) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", x[1, "EstimatedMean"], sqrt(v[1, "EstimatedVar"]))
  counts <- function(column) dsBaseClient::ds.table(paste0("D_baseline$", column),
    useNA = "always", datasources = connections)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
  sex <- counts("sex"); bands <- counts("age_band")
  cell <- function(numerator) sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", numerator, 100 * numerator / n)
  c(People = as.character(n),
    `Age, years: mean (SD)` = numeric_text(age, variance("age")),
    `Age missing, n` = as.character(age[1, "Nmissing"]),
    `Female, n (%)` = cell(sex[["F"]]), `Male, n (%)` = cell(sex[["M"]]),
    `Sex missing, n (%)` = cell(sex[["NA"]]),
    `Under 18, n (%)` = cell(bands[["under 18"]]), `Adult, n (%)` = cell(bands[["adult"]]),
    `Age group missing, n (%)` = cell(bands[["NA"]]),
    `Baseline haemoglobin, g/dL: mean (SD)` = numeric_text(lab, variance("haemoglobin")),
    `Haemoglobin missing, n` = as.character(lab[1, "Nmissing"]))
}
site_a <- describe(two_conns[1])
site_b <- describe(two_conns[2])
total <- describe(two_conns)
data.frame(Characteristic = names(total), north = unname(site_a),
  south = unname(site_b), Total = unname(total))
Characteristic north south Total
People 14 14 28
Age, years: mean (SD) 18.64 (19.44) 25.36 (20.13) 22.00 (19.71)
Age missing, n 0 0 0
Female, n (%) 4 (28.6%) 9 (64.3%) 13 (46.4%)
Male, n (%) 10 (71.4%) 5 (35.7%) 15 (53.6%)
Sex missing, n (%) 0 (0.0%) 0 (0.0%) 0 (0.0%)
Under 18, n (%) 7 (50.0%) 6 (42.9%) 13 (46.4%)
Adult, n (%) 7 (50.0%) 8 (57.1%) 15 (53.6%)
Age group missing, n (%) 0 (0.0%) 0 (0.0%) 0 (0.0%)
Baseline haemoglobin, g/dL: mean (SD) 14.01 (1.62) 13.96 (2.53) 13.99 (2.08)
Haemoglobin missing, n 0 0 0

Each site contributes 14 people, for 28 total. The sites differ: female counts are 4 (28.6%) and 9 (64.3%). Mean completed age is 18.64 and 25.36 years, with pooled mean 22.00. Pooled baseline haemoglobin is 13.99 g/dL, not the all-history mean 14.47. Missing rows state the denominator for each variable; a withheld cell must never be silently filled with zero.

The total SD includes both within-site and between-site variation. It is not obtained by averaging site SDs. Site columns make population differences visible that a pooled column alone would hide.

Exercises

1. Detect future information. Replace baseline haemoglobin with the mean over all history, keeping the same first-haemoglobin population. Quantify the difference.

Solution 1

all_history <- omop_study(hb, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(
  baseline = omop_value_at_index("measurement", hb_set, tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(8713L)),
  history = omop_variable(event = hb, reducer = omop_reduce("mean"))))
recipe_execute(all_history, out = c(baseline = "D_history"), conns = two_conns)
ds.omop.mutate("D_history", difference = history - baseline,
  newobj = "D_history_difference", conns = two_conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.mean("D_history_difference$difference", type = "combine", datasources = two_conns)$Global.Mean
EstimatedMean Nmissing Nvalid Ntotal
studiesCombined 0.481 0 28 28

The mean difference is about 0.481 g/dL. The all-history mean includes later readings for 25 people and therefore cannot be used as a baseline characteristic.

2. Add a common haemoglobin category. Use a public teaching cutoff of 14 g/dL and show the counts separately at each site. Do equal definitions imply equal counts?

Solution 2

bands <- omop_study(hb, outputs = "baseline", baseline = list(
  band = omop_number_bins(omop_value_at_index("measurement", hb_set,
    tolerance = c(0, 0), unit = omop_unit(8713L)),
    breaks = c(-Inf, 14, Inf), labels = c("below 14", "14 or above"))))
recipe_execute(bands, out = c(baseline = "D_baseline_bands"), conns = two_conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_baseline_bands$band",
  datasources = two_conns)$output.list$TABLE_rvar.by.study_counts
north south
below 14 8 7
14 or above 6 7
NA 0 0

Both sites use the same boundary and labels. Counts depend on their people; sharing a definition makes comparison meaningful without forcing distributions to match. The cutoff is a teaching rule, not a clinical reference interval.

Recap

Describe the population at a shared entry point, keep future information out of baseline variables, and show each site beside the total. Report missingness and use pooled variance for the total SD.
